mainTopic: Festival gifts to non-Jews who do not serve idols, and wages or rental fees connected to יין נסך.
overview: The amud opens with רב יהודה, who sent a gift to a non-Jew named אבידרנא on his festival day because he knew the man does not serve idols. רב יוסף challenges him twice from the laws of a גר תושב, and רב יהודה answers both challenges. Next, רבא sends a gift to בר שישך for the same reason. Their talk turns into a debate about whether עולם הבא can beat worldly pleasure, and the story ends with בר שישך's own curse striking him. רב פפי and רב נחמן בר יצחק then suggest פסוקים that רבא could have quoted. The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks when a worker's wage stays permitted if he was also asked to move יין נסך. אביי and רבא give two answers, and a ברייתא supports רבא. The גמרא then discusses renting a donkey: a jug the renter adds does not change the fee, and it explains what the renter and the donkey driver may each load. The amud ends as a new story about the father of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא begins.

steps.title: רב יהודה's gift to אבידרנא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה sent a gift to אבידרנא on his festival day, because he knew this man does not serve idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רב יהודה sent a gift] to אבידרנא on their festival day. He said: I know about him that he does not worship idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes telling us that רב יהודה sent a gift to a non-Jew on his holiday, and it gives his reason: this man does not serve idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually it is forbidden to give a gift to an idol worshipper on his festival, because he may go and thank his idol for it. רב יהודה says that this rule does not apply to someone he personally knows does not serve idols. This reasoning is what רב יוסף is about to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Their festival day, the holiday of the idol worshippers

phrases.english: to Avidarna on their festival day.
He said: I know about him
that he does not worship idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר: ידענא ביה דלא פלח לעבודה זרה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section. It continues the story of רב יהודה from the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who is known not to serve idols may be given a gift on the festival day.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a גר תושב needs a formal acceptance
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא: a גר תושב is only someone who formally accepted, in front of three חברים, not to serve idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: But it was taught in a ברייתא: Who is a גר תושב? Anyone who accepted upon himself, in front of three חברים, not to worship idols!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רב יהודה. He argues that a non-Jew only gets special status if he formally promises in front of three חברים, and אבידרנא never did that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה relied on his private knowledge of how the man behaves. The ברייתא seems to say that only a formal acceptance in front of three חברים counts. If so, אבידרנא should still be treated like any other non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: A resident non-Jew who gave up idol worship but did not fully convert

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
But isn't it taught: Who is a ger toshav?
Anyone who has accepted upon himself
before three haverim
not to worship idols!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רב יוסף: והתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of רב יהודה in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that private knowledge that the man does not serve idols is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines non-idolater status (גר תושב) by a formal acceptance in front of three חברים. אבידרנא never made one, so he should not count.

steps.title: That rule is about supporting him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's requirement of three חברים is only for the duty to support a גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about keeping him alive (supporting him).
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that the ברייתא is talking about a different law: when we are obligated to support and sustain a גר תושב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formal acceptance is needed before we must actively help and support someone. For the gift rule, the only question is whether he will thank an idol, so knowing that he does not serve idols is enough. The same word, גר תושב, can have different requirements for different laws.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep him alive, to support and sustain him

phrases.english: When that was taught — it was regarding sustaining him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is a גר תושב: we have to help him make a living and survive among us.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי תניא ההיא — להחיותו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a different law (אוקימתא by topic).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא defines non-idolater status for every law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The formal acceptance is only needed for the duty to support him. For the gift rule, private knowledge is enough.

steps.title: A גר תושב who did not circumcise is like a מין
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges again: רבי יוחנן said that a גר תושב who goes twelve months without מילה is like a מין, and אבידרנא is certainly not circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A גר תושב who has gone twelve months without circumcising is like a heretic among the nations!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge: if even a real גר תושב loses his status after a year without מילה, then an uncircumcised man like אבידרנא surely has no special status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge suggests that refusing מילה shows bad faith and turns the non-Jew into a מין. If so, private knowledge that he does not serve idols should not help אבידרנא.

keyTerms.meaning: And he did not circumcise himself

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabba bar bar Hana say
phrases.notes: The challenger is not named again. It is still רב יוסף pushing back.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yohanan says:
A ger toshav for whom have passed
twelve months and he did not circumcise himself,
is like a heretic among the nations!

steps.triggerLanguage: והאמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, new challenge to רב יהודה, after step 3 answered the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's treatment of אבידרנא as a non-idolater.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a גר תושב who stays uncircumcised for a year is like a מין, then an uncircumcised non-Jew cannot get favorable treatment.

steps.title: Only when he promised to circumcise and didn't
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's rule is about someone who agreed to circumcise and then backed out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a case where he accepted upon himself to circumcise and did not circumcise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that רבי יוחנן is only talking about a man who promised to do מילה and then broke his promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking that promise is what shows he is a מין. A non-Jew who never took מילה upon himself is not required to do it, so being uncircumcised says nothing bad about אבידרנא. רב יהודה's gift stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as (narrows the case)

steps.whatToRemember: Private knowledge that a non-Jew does not serve idols is enough to allow a gift on his festival. The formal acceptance in front of three חברים is for the duty to support him, and the twelve-month rule is only for someone who promised מילה and broke his word.

phrases.english: There, it is a case where he accepted upon himself
to circumcise, and did not circumcise.

steps.triggerLanguage: התם כגון שקיבל עליו למול ולא מל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any uncircumcised גר תושב becomes like a מין after a year.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one who took מילה upon himself and backed out becomes like a מין.

steps.title: רבא sends a gift to בר שישך
steps.stepSummary: רבא also sent a gift on the festival day to a non-Jew, בר שישך, using the same reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא brought a gift to בר שישך on their festival day. He said: I know about him that he does not worship idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story with the same pattern as רב יהודה's: רבא gave a gift on the festival because he knew the man did not serve idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows that רבא held the same view as רב יהודה. The story then moves into a conversation between them.
steps.confusionAlert: Here קורבנא means a gift to an important person, not a sacrifice in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rava brought a gift
to bar Sheshakh on their festival day.
He said: I know about him
that he does not worship idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמטי ליה קורבנא לבר שישך ביום אידם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא also allowed a festival gift to a non-Jew he knew did not serve idols.

steps.title: רבא finds him in luxury
steps.stepSummary: רבא arrives and finds בר שישך soaking in rose water up to his neck, with immoral women standing in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and found him sitting up to his neck in rose water, and naked prostitutes were standing before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story sets the scene: בר שישך is living a life of wild pleasure. This sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture of extreme luxury is the background for בר שישך's question. He will boast that this is the best life there is.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: He went and found him
sitting up to his neck in roses,
phrases.notes: He means a bath of rose water, a sign of huge wealth.

phrases.english: and naked prostitutes were standing before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אזל אשכחיה דיתיב עד צואריה בוורדא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setting: בר שישך lives in extreme pleasure.

steps.title: Do you have this in the World to Come?
steps.stepSummary: בר שישך asks רבא whether the Jews will have pleasures like this in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you have anything like this in the World to Come?
steps.whatsHappening: בר שישך asks a mocking question. He is suggesting that his life now beats anything the Jews hope for later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His idea is that physical pleasure is the highest good. He is challenging whether the Jewish reward in עולם הבא could compare.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this, something of this kind

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִית לְכוּ כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you have something like this
in the World to Come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: אית לכו כהאי גוונא לעלמא דאתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בר שישך reacts to his own luxury described in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the Jews' reward in עולם הבא matches this pleasure.

steps.title: Ours is better
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that what the Jews will have is even better.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Ours is much better than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers simply: the reward of עולם הבא is greater than all this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not explain yet why it is better. This leads to בר שישך's next question.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּידַן עֲדִיפָא טְפֵי מֵהַאי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Ours is much better than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: דידן עדיפא טפי מהאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Jews' reward in עולם הבא is better than this.

steps.title: Can anything beat this?
steps.stepSummary: בר שישך doubts that anything could be better than his pleasures.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Can there be anything better than this?
steps.whatsHappening: בר שישך pushes back. He cannot imagine anything better than what he has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This pushes רבא to explain what makes עולם הבא better. It sets up רבא's real answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טְפֵי מֵהַאי מִי הָוֵה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Can there be more than this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: טפי מהאי מי הוה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the Jews' reward is better.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing can be imagined that is better than this level of pleasure.

steps.title: No fear of the government
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains: you live under fear of the government, but we will have no such fear in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have the fear of the government upon you; we will not have the fear of the government upon us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his reason: all of בר שישך's pleasure is spoiled by fear of the king, while עולם הבא has no such fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pleasure that can be taken away at any moment is not complete. The reward of עולם הבא is complete and safe, so it is better.

phrases.english: He said to him: You have upon you
the fear of the government;
we will not have upon us
the fear of the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: אתון איכא עלייכו אימתא דמלכותא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולם הבא is better because it has no fear of the government.

steps.title: What fear do I have?
steps.stepSummary: בר שישך insists that he, a powerful man, has no fear of the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As for me, at least, what fear of the government is there on me?
steps.whatsHappening: בר שישך rejects רבא's point. He says he is so powerful that the government does not scare him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is attacking the premise of רבא's answer, claiming his pleasure has no fear in it. The story will now show him wrong.

phrases.english: He said to him: As for me, at least,
what fear of the government is there upon me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: אנא מיהא מאי אימתא דמלכותא איכא עלי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that בר שישך lives under fear of the government.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בר שישך is powerful, so he says he has nothing to fear.

steps.title: The king's officer arrives
steps.stepSummary: Right then a royal officer comes and orders בר שישך to get up because the king is calling him.
steps.simpleTranslation: While they were sitting, a royal officer came and said to him: Get up, the king wants you.
steps.whatsHappening: The events themselves prove רבא right: at that very moment the king summons בר שישך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר שישך has to leave his pleasures immediately when the king calls. This shows he really is under the fear of the government.

phrases.english: While they were sitting,
a certain royal officer of the king came,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם, דְּקָבָעֵי לָךְ מַלְכָּא.
phrases.english: and said to him: Get up, for the king wants you.

steps.triggerLanguage: עד דיתבי אתא ההוא פריסתקא דמלכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The events refute בר שישך's claim in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that בר שישך lives under fear of the government.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The king suddenly summons בר שישך in the middle of his pleasure.

steps.title: The curse turns back on בר שישך
steps.stepSummary: Leaving, בר שישך says, 'May the eye that wants to see you harmed burst.' רבא answers 'Amen,' and בר שישך's own eye bursts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he was going out, he said to him: May the eye that wants to see evil come to you burst. רבא said to him: Amen. בר שישך's eye burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with בר שישך admitting רבא was right, and his own words turning back on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he saw that רבא was right, בר שישך cursed anyone who wishes the Jews harm. רבא answered 'Amen,' and the curse struck בר שישך's own eye, hinting that he was the one with an evil eye toward them.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא, like רב יהודה, allowed a festival gift to someone known not to serve idols. The story shows that the reward of עולם הבא is better than any worldly pleasure, because worldly pleasure always comes with fear.

phrases.english: As he was going out, he said to him:
The eye that wishes to see evil upon you
phrases.notes: Literally "upon you all": he means רבא and the Jewish people.

phrases.english: should burst.
Rava said to him: Amen.
The eye of bar Sheshakh burst.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי נפיק ואזיל אמר ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story begun in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בר שישך admits that רבא was right, and his own curse falls on himself.

steps.title: רב פפי offers a better verse for רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי says רבא could have answered בר שישך with a פסוק that says kings' daughters will honor the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: רבא should have answered him with this verse: 'Kings' daughters are among your favorites; at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir.'
steps.whatsHappening: Looking back at the story, רב פפי suggests a stronger answer רבא could have given בר שישך. It is a פסוק showing that royal honor awaits the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר שישך bragged that nothing could be better than his royal pleasures. רב פפי says a פסוק showing that kings' daughters will stand in honor before Israel answers that boast directly. He is not saying רבא was wrong, only that this answer fits the boast more closely.

keyTerms.meaning: He should have said (he had a better answer available)
Gold of Ophir, the finest gold

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
He should have said to him
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, and "him" is בר שישך from the story we just finished.

phrases.english: from this verse:
"Kings' daughters are among your favorites;
at your right hand stands the queen in gold of Ophir."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמֵימְרָא לֵיהּ מֵהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the story after it ends, offering a better answer to בר שישך's boast
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסוק about kings' daughters honoring Israel would have answered בר שישך's claim more directly

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers another verse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the best answer is the פסוק that says no eye has seen the reward waiting for those who hope for God.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He should have answered him from here: 'No eye has seen it, God, except You, what He will do for those who wait for Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers a different פסוק that רבא could have used. This one says the reward of עולם הבא is beyond anything a person has ever seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי compared the reward to royal honor. רב נחמן בר יצחק goes further: the reward is so great that no human eye has ever seen anything like it. So it cannot be measured against בר שישך's pleasures at all.

keyTerms.meaning: For the one who waits for Him

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends by teaching that the reward of עולם הבא is beyond any pleasure in this world, even a king's.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
He should have said to him from here:
"No eye has seen it, God, except You,
what He will do for the one who waits for Him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמֵימְרָא לֵיהּ מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, competing verse instead of רב פפי's
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward of עולם הבא is beyond anything ever seen, so it is greater than any pleasure in this world

steps.title: Back to the משנה: hired for other work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a worker hired for other work, and points out that the wage seems permitted even if he was asked to move the יין נסך in the middle of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he hired him to do other work with him,' his wage is permitted. This is true even if he did not ask him toward evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and returns to the משנה. It points out something about the משנה's wording, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if a non-Jew hired a Jew for other work and also asked him to move a barrel of יין נסך, the wage is permitted. The משנה does not mention the time of day. So it seems the wage is permitted even if the request came in the middle of the workday.

keyTerms.meaning: Hired him (here); the same word can also mean 'his wage'
Other work (not involving the forbidden wine)
Toward evening, near the end of the workday

steps.confusionAlert: The word שְׂכָרוֹ means 'he hired him' in this line. In the ברייתא in the next step, it means 'his wage.' Same word, two meanings.

phrases.english: If he hired him to do other work with him.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The non-Jew hired the Jew, and during the work also asked him to move a barrel of יין נסך.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ
phrases.english: And even though he did not tell him
toward evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂכָרוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת עִמּוֹ מְלָאכָה אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the halachic discussion of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's wording, the wage is permitted even when the request to move the wine did not come toward evening

steps.title: A ברייתא says only toward evening
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits the wage when the worker was asked toward evening, which implies it would be forbidden during the day. This contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction: 'One who hires a worker, and toward evening says to him: Move a barrel of יין נסך from place to place, his wage is permitted.' The reason is that he asked him toward evening. Yes, then it is permitted; during the whole day, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite of the משנה. It allows the wage only when the request came at the end of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא specifically says 'toward evening,' so that detail must matter. Toward evening, the paid work is already done, so the wage is clearly not payment for moving the wine. During the day, the wage would be mixed with payment for the forbidden job. That clashes with what we read in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction (between two sources)
Wine poured or used for idol worship, forbidden for any benefit
The reason (the ruling depends on this detail)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
One who hires a worker,
and toward evening said to him:
"Move a barrel of wine used for idol worship
from place to place,"
his wage is permitted.
The reason is that he told him toward evening:
then yes; during the whole day, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from the משנה with a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the משנה permits the wage even without the request coming toward evening
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's 'toward evening' implies that a request during the day makes the wage forbidden, contradicting the משנה

steps.title: אביי: the משנה also means toward evening
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is also talking about a request made toward evening, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When we learned the משנה too, we learned it about a case where he asked toward evening.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction by reading the משנה the same way as the ברייתא. Both are talking about a request made at the end of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in step 17 came only from the משנה not mentioning the time. אביי says the משנה simply left the detail out. It really also means toward evening, so both sources agree that during the day the wage would be forbidden.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When we learned our משנה too,
we learned it about where he said this toward evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restricting the case of the משנה to match the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה permits the wage even when the request came during the day
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה also refers only to a request made toward evening

steps.title: רבא: it depends on how he is paid
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the two sources deal with different payment setups. One price for a hundred barrels makes the whole wage forbidden, while a separate פרוטה per barrel keeps the wage permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is no difficulty. This source is where he told him, 'Move a hundred barrels for me for a hundred פרוטות.' That source is where he told him, 'Move each barrel for me for one פרוטה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He keeps the משנה as it is and says the two sources are about different kinds of work deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worker is paid one price for all hundred barrels, it is one single job. If one barrel is יין נסך, the whole wage is mixed with the forbidden work, so it is permitted only toward evening, as the ברייתא says. If each barrel is paid separately, each barrel is its own job, so the rest of the wage is permitted even during the day, as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the two sources do not really clash)
This one... that one (each source refers to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says both sources mean toward evening. רבא says it depends on payment: one price for the whole job (ברייתא) versus a price per barrel (משנה).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer shows that whether work counts as one job or many separate jobs decides whether a forbidden part spoils the whole wage.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult.
This is where he said to him:
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא, where the wage is permitted only toward evening.

phrases.english: "Move for me a hundred barrels for a hundred perutot,"
that is where he said to him:
phrases.notes: "That" is our משנה, where the wage is permitted at any time.

phrases.english: "Move for me each barrel for one peruta."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction instead of אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא are talking about the same kind of deal
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about one price for the whole job; the משנה is about a separate price for each barrel

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא's distinction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules exactly as רבא said. If the worker was paid one price for a hundred barrels, the whole wage is forbidden. If he was paid a פרוטה per barrel, the wage is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it is taught in a ברייתא: Someone hired a worker and told him, 'Move a hundred barrels for me for a hundred פרוטות,' and a barrel of יין נסך turned up among them. The wage is forbidden. If he said 'each barrel for a פרוטה,' and a barrel of יין נסך turned up among them, the wage is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבא's answer from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one combined price, the payment for the forbidden barrel cannot be separated out, so the whole wage is forbidden. When each barrel has its own פרוטה, only that one פרוטה is tied to the יין נסך, so the rest of the wage is fine. This is exactly the line רבא drew.
steps.whatToRemember: One combined price makes the whole wage forbidden. A separate price for each barrel keeps the wage permitted.

phrases.english: And so it is taught: One who hires a worker,
and said to him: 'Move for me'
a hundred barrels for a hundred perutot,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצֵאת חָבִית שֶׁל יֵין נֶסֶךְ בֵּינֵיהֶן —
phrases.english: and a barrel of libation wine was found among them
his wage is forbidden.
Each barrel for a peruta,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצֵאת חָבִית שֶׁל יֵין נֶסֶךְ בֵּינֵיהֶן —
phrases.english: and a barrel of libation wine was found among them
his wage is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer from step 20
steps.raayaObject: רבא's distinction between one total price and a price per barrel
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same two payment cases and the same rulings

steps.title: The משנה's case of a donkey rented to carry יין נסך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if a גוי rents a Jew's donkey to carry יין נסך, the rental fee is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a donkey to carry יין נסך on it, the fee is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It quotes the line to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rental fee is payment for carrying the forbidden wine, so the money is forbidden. The rule itself is simple. What the גמרא wants to ask about is why the משנה needed to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured or used for idol worship

phrases.english: One who rents a donkey
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. A גוי is renting a Jew's donkey.

phrases.english: to carry libation wine on it
its fee is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fee for renting out a donkey to carry יין נסך is forbidden

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat the same rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this line is needed, since it seems to be the same rule as the first case of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this line too? It is the same as the first case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case already taught that getting paid to carry יין נסך makes the wage forbidden. Whether a worker or a donkey does the carrying, the idea is the same. So this line looks like it adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this as well?
That is the same as the first case

phrases.english: Why do I need this as well?
This is the same as the first clause!
phrases.notes: The first clause is the משנה's case of a worker paid to carry יין נסך.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה line quoted in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The donkey line in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It repeats the same idea as the first case, so it seems unnecessary

steps.title: The line is there for the riding case that follows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needed the donkey case for the next part. If the donkey was rented for riding, the fee is permitted even if the גוי put his jug of יין נסך on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part was needed: if he rented it to ride on, even though the גוי put his jug on it, the fee is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה said the donkey case in order to set up the next case, which is really new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is about what the fee pays for. The donkey was rented for riding, not for carrying wine. So the jug the גוי added on his own is not part of what he paid for, and the fee stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part was what he needed

phrases.english: The latter clause was necessary for him:
if he rented it to sit on it,
even though the gentile placed
his jug on it
phrases.notes: He means a jug of יין נסך.

phrases.english: its fee is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: The line is a lead-in that sets up a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The donkey line just repeats the first case
steps.terutzMaskana: It sets up the riding case, where the fee is permitted even with a jug on the donkey

steps.title: Does a renter have no right to load a jug?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this means a renter has no right to put a jug on the donkey, so the jug is not covered by the fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that a renter does not have the right to place a jug on the donkey?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what the last answer seems to assume. This sets up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fee is permitted only if the jug was not part of what the rental paid for. That seems to mean a renter normally has no right to load a jug on the donkey. The גמרא is checking whether that is really true.

phrases.english: Is this to say that a jug
he has no legal right to place it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא, דְּלָגִין לָאו דִּינָא הוּא לְאוֹתוֹבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what step 24's answer assumes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a renter normally has no right to load a jug on a rented donkey

steps.title: A ברייתא says a renter may load his jug
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists what a renter and a donkey driver may each put on the donkey. The renter may load his jug, which contradicts the idea from the last step.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: When someone rents a donkey, the renter may put on it his garment, his jug, and his food for that trip. Beyond that, the donkey driver may stop him. The donkey driver may put on it barley and straw and his food for that day. Beyond that, the renter may stop him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a ברייתא that seems to clash with the assumption from step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly says the renter may put his water jug on the donkey. So the jug is part of what a rental includes. That would mean the fee also pays for carrying the jug, which challenges the answer that the fee stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: May stop him / hold him back

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people here. The שוכר is the one renting the donkey. The חמר is the owner's driver who leads the donkey. Each one may stop the other from overloading it.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: One who rents a donkey
the renter may place on it
his garment and his jug
and his food for that journey;
beyond this, the donkey driver may stop him.
The donkey driver may place on it
barley and straw
and his food for that day;
beyond this, the renter may stop him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption raised in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a renter has no right to load a jug, which step 24's answer depends on
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a renter may load his jug, so the jug is included in the rental fee

steps.title: אביי: The Fee Doesn't Change Because of the Jug
steps.stepSummary: אביי agrees that a renter may put a jug on the donkey. But nobody lowers the price when he doesn't, so no part of the fee is paying for the jug of יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: True, the renter has a right to put a jug on the donkey. But if he does not put one on, do we tell the owner, 'Take off the cost of his jug from the fee'? No. So the fee is not paying for the jug.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from the ברייתא in the last step. He agrees the renter may load a jug, but shows that the fee is still permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether the fee partly pays for carrying the יין נסך. אביי says the jug is only a free extra that comes with the ride, because the price is the same with or without it. Since no money is tied to the jug, the fee is not 'payment for יין נסך' and stays permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's ruling that a donkey rented for riding brings a permitted fee, even if the גוי put his jug of יין נסך on it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Granted that it is the renter's legal right to place a jug on the donkey,
still, if he does not place it there,
do we say to the owner:
'Deduct from the rental the fee for his jug'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְהִי דְּלָגִין דִּינָא הוּא לְאוֹתוֹבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised from the ברייתא in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the ברייתא's fact (the renter may load a jug) but shows it does not affect the price.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the renter has a right to load a jug, part of the fee would be paying for carrying the יין נסך.
steps.terutzMaskana: The jug costs nothing extra, since the fee is never lowered without it. So the fee is not payment for the wine and is permitted.

steps.title: When Does the Renter-Driver Difference Make Sense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's difference between the renter and the חמר about food. If food is easy to buy on the road, neither needs to carry it. If it is hard to buy, both should be allowed to carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is easy to buy food along the way, the driver should also be able to stop the renter from loading food. And if it is not easy to buy food along the way, the renter should also not be able to stop the driver from loading food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the ברייתא from step 26 and asks what kind of road it is talking about. It shows that both options seem to give the same rule for the renter and the חמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא let the renter load his food for the whole trip, but limited the חמר to food for that day. The גמרא says the rule should be the same for both: if food can be bought on the way, neither needs to carry extra. If it can't, both should carry extra. So why treat them differently?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If places to buy food along the way are common,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא from step 26: the renter may load food for the whole trip, the driver only for that day.

phrases.english: then the driver should also be able to stop the renter from loading food,
and if places to buy food are not common,
then the renter should also not be able to stop the driver from loading food.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דִּשְׁכִיחַ לְמִזְבַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יין נסך question and asks about the ברייתא quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's different rules for the renter and the חמר about carrying food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whatever the road is like, the logic gives the same answer for both people. So the difference between them seems to have no basis.

steps.title: רב פפא: Food Can Be Bought, but It Takes Effort
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ברייתא is about a road where food can be bought from station to station, but only with effort. A חמר is used to that effort, so he may not load extra food. A renter is not used to it, so he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The ruling is needed for a case where you can buy food from station to station, but only by making an effort. A driver is used to making the effort to buy. A renter is not used to making the effort to buy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by describing a middle case. In this case the renter and the חמר really are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only looked at two options: food is easy to buy, or it is not available. רב פפא adds a third case: food is available, but buying it takes work. Since drivers travel this way all the time and are used to that work, they are held to it. Renters are not used to it, so they may bring all their food along.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this specific case)
To make an effort, to trouble oneself
A stopping station or inn along the road
His usual way, what he is used to

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's rule fits a road where food can be bought along the way, but only with effort. The חמר is expected to make that effort. The renter is not.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is needed only
where it is possible to make an effort and buy food
from station to station,
a driver is used to making the effort to buy,
a renter is not used to making the effort to buy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא צְרִיכָא דִּשְׁכִיחַ לְמִיטְרַח וּלְמִזְבַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle case, where food can be bought but only with effort, in which the two people differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only options are that food is easy to buy or not available, and both give the same rule for renter and חמר.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the middle case, the חמר is used to the effort and must buy along the way. The renter is not, so he may load food for the whole trip.

steps.title: A New Story Begins: The Father of רב אחא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about the father of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא. The story continues on the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new story about the father of רב אחא בריה דרב איקא, and the story continues right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא now turns to a real-life case. For now, we only learn who the story is about. What he did and the ruling will come next.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
phrases.english: The father of Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after the discussion of the ברייתא has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces who the story is about.
